newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close slightly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose mildly on Thursday in thin trading with most activity concentrated in unlinked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 104.00
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 to 103.16
Volume was a low 97 million shekels.
"The market was very quiet today. Activity always falls before long weekends. Investors simply prefer to wait until Monday," one trader said.
The market will be closed on Sunday because of the Jewish holiday of Purim.
"CPI-linked long bonds rose today, but activity in inflation-linked bonds was relatively low," said a trader at IBI Investment House.
She said most activity was concentrated in unlinked bonds. "Yields on CPI-linked short bonds fell to only 3.8 percent so investors moved to unlinked bonds," she said.
Traders noted that the Makam rose slightly on volume of only 16 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds were today's main losers after the shekel rose against the dollar for the second day. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3600 shekels against 3.3650 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
